title: Chapter 45: Someone Is Trying to Kill Me!
html:
Within a minute, the comment section erupted again.

“That shadow leaning against the tub near the end is a special effect, right? It looks like it crawls out from below.”

“The host’s reaction sells it. Either that is excellent acting or he genuinely did not expect the shadow.”

“If that thing had held on any longer, this would have stopped being entertainment.”

“I was watching casually until the shadow appeared. Now every dark corner of my room looks suspicious.”

“Run while you still can! This account posts nothing but ghost videos!”

“I stared at my phone for one minute and somehow lost the ability to sleep.”

“Your last video ruined mirrors for me, and now you have ruined bathrooms too. Heartless host.”

Chen Ge was pleased that the clip had received such a strong response even at that hour. Before closing the app, he slipped in an advertisement for the Haunted House. His followers immediately promised to visit—and, with characteristic enthusiasm, to bring him various “local specialties.”

They buy tickets to visit the Haunted House and still want to bring me gifts. My visitors really are generous.

After closing the app, Chen Ge felt considerably better. He stretched, gathered the five dolls against his chest, and left Murder by Midnight.

Night gave way to dawn, and pale light crept across the Haunted House. Chen Ge found several wooden planks in the props room and sealed both the main entrance and the concealed access point to Murder by Midnight. Until he dealt with the mirror entity, the scenario would remain closed.

Twenty yuan a ticket, seven visitors per run, roughly four runs an hour… Closing this scenario is going to cost me a painful amount of money.

The thought hurt, but greed did not override common sense.Safety first. There will be more money to earn once I unlock other scenarios.

With the scenario secured, Chen Ge returned to the staff break room, set the dolls beside his bed, and changed into running clothes. The recent Trial Mission had reminded him how much his occasional training mattered when things went wrong.

Xu Wan arrived around 8:40 a.m. and was surprised to find her boss returning from a run, his hair damp with sweat. In her experience, exercise was not one of Chen Ge’s hobbies.

When the Haunted House gates opened, another workday began. Chen Ge and Xu Wan took their usual positions. Visitors started entering the park at nine, but the area in front of the Haunted House remained one of New Century Park’s quietest corners.

“Boss, what happened in there last night? Why are there puddles everywhere?”

“I was mopping the floor,” Chen Ge improvised. Then, more seriously, he added, “When you’re working inside, stay away from the mirrors for now.”

“Why?”

Before Chen Ge could think of an explanation, he spotted Uncle Xu approaching from across the park.

“Uncle Xu, something wrong?” Chen Ge removed his headset. The older man did not look pleased.

“You get stranger every day.” Uncle Xu looked him up and down. “The canteen staff reported some missing kitchen equipment this morning. Security footage showed you wandering in there in the middle of the night and taking it. Would you like to explain what you were doing?”

Only then did Chen Ge remember the canteen equipment he had borrowed and left in the bathroom.

“I needed something for an emergency last night,” he said, choosing his words carefully. “I’ll replace everything I borrowed. I promise.”

Considering what had happened in the bathroom, returning the items to food service seemed like a terrible idea. Replacing them was safer for everyone.

“It is becoming harder and harder to understand you.” Uncle Xu narrowed his eyes. “Tell me the truth. You are not mixed up in anything illegal, are you?”

“Nothing illegal, Uncle Xu. Strange, yes. Illegal, no.”

Uncle Xu looked only half convinced. The park had just opened, however, and he had too much to do to interrogate Chen Ge properly. He stepped closer and handed him a tightly wrapped envelope. “Here is the five thousand yuan you asked for. If you are in real trouble, come to me instead of handling everything yourself.”

“Thank you, Uncle Xu. I’ll pay you back this weekend.”

“Stay out of trouble. I’ll count that as interest.”

After Uncle Xu left, Chen Ge tucked the money safely away and leaned against the entrance, considering how best to use it.

Five thousand should cover a basic camera system. But the Haunted House is already full. I need more space before I can unlock new scenarios. The underground parking area still seems like the best option—assuming management will rent it to me at a reasonable price.

The list of problems was long enough to give him a headache.And every problem comes back to the same thing: money. The police reward still has not arrived. Should I ask about it?

His gaze drifted toward the direction of the police station, then stopped on a visitor at the edge of the park. The man wore a cap pulled low and a long-sleeved top despite the mild weather. Both hands remained tucked in his pockets as he wandered between attractions without seeming interested in any of them.

He looks familiar.

Yin Yang Vision had sharpened Chen Ge’s eyesight enough that he could study the stranger from a distance. The man appeared unaware that he had been noticed.

Should I stop him?

Before Chen Ge could decide, a group of visitors arrived for the Haunted House. Work distracted him, and the stranger slipped from his thoughts. Near lunchtime, however, Chen Ge spotted the same man loitering nearby again.

He avoided the Haunted House all morning, and now he comes over just as Xiao Wan and I are leaving for lunch. What is he waiting for?

Chen Ge told Xu Wan to go ahead and returned to the entrance. The moment the stranger noticed him, the man turned away and left the park without looking back.

Where have I seen him before?

Unease settled over him. He skipped lunch and went to the park’s security office. With the guards’ permission, he reviewed the day’s camera footage.

The stranger seemed to avoid cameras whenever he could. He kept one hand hidden almost constantly and, despite paying admission, had visited only one attraction: the Ferris wheel, three times in succession.

That is not normal sightseeing.
